The Solutrean Origin hypothesis for the origins and spread of Clovis culture into the New World has never gained a large following among archaeologists. The model holds that early dispersals into the New World from Siberia were supplemented by dispersals from Europe across the Atlantic (Bradley and Stanford, 2004). The model is built upon supposed similarities between Clovis lithic technology and the Upper Paleolithic Solutrean technologies of Western Europe (Bradley and Stanford, 2004; Boldurian and Cotter, 1999; Greenman, 1963). This route would necessitate a heavy reliance on sea faring technology, as no land bridge has ever connected Europe and North America during human history.
